value.subject: github-actions-scheduler
value.obligation: incident-github-dispatch-delay: GitHub cron is not the freshness clock (RULING 218); stand up the runtime scheduler on the decided Postgres provider (RULING 220) so ordinary civic-data movement leaves the commit path — Session B executes
value.why: Measured evidence, recorded as tracker rows JOB07-JOB18 and docs/log.md: scheduled dispatch delays of 186.5 min (job-watch.yml, slot 2026-08-30T15:40Z, run 33329026985), 256.6 min (intake-tripwire.yml, slot 2026-08-30T10:41Z, run 33318287070), 313.1 min (refresh-daily.yml, slot 2026-08-30T09:11Z, run 33316760622); typical delays 186-638 min across 2026-08-27..30; largest single observation 698.2 min (run 33209856186, slot 2026-08-28T09:11Z); observation envelope 699 min over 9 scheduled runs — a floor that grows, never a ceiling. All delays are dispatch delay, not runner queueing: startedAt equals createdAt on every read. A refresh landing ten hours after its slot serves day-old data while every failure counter reports healthy. This is a freshness-architecture defect, not an owner decision.
